opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions up to £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections up to £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications up to £5,000; Long-Term Research grants up to £20,000; Research and Travel grants up to £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating as non-profit for at least 12 months) for most categories; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category. Applications from individuals independently wishing to create/inform/develop their own practice are not accepted.
opportunities.summary: Henry Moore Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and fund research that expands the appreciation of sculpture. Categories: New Projects and Commissions (exhibitions, catalogues, commissions), Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, Long-Term Research, and Research and Travel. Applications are considered four times per year (Autumn, Winter, Spring, Summer rounds).

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation for travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, rest of world up to £1,000; plus accommodation provided in Leeds or Hertfordshire

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics or curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships); researchers whose interests lie specifically in Henry Moore (Studios & Gardens fellowships); artists developing their practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars for six-week Senior Fellowships.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enable artists and researchers to spend a month using the Foundation's research facilities in Leeds (Henry Moore Institute) or Hertfordshire (Henry Moore Studios & Gardens), including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications for 2026/27 are closed; the next round of fellowship applications opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize each for BA and MA dissertations, plus Henry Moore Institute publications to the value of £50 and publication of dissertation abstracts

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Each year the Institute awards two prizes for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture (one BA and one MA dissertation). Submissions should have a strong focus on secondary and primary sources and original research. The 2025 prize deadline has passed; submissions for the 2026 prize open in autumn.
